narrative: Material PL1__MA783317 exhibits variable but largely continuous demand averaging 321 units per working day (CV=0.67) with no statistically significant trend over the observed period March 2025 to March 2026. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.68, mean 1.56 days) and constitute the dominant source of buffer variance, driving safety stock requirements significantly above the current SAP setting of 208 units. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended, with a reorder point of 1,295 units and EOQ-derived order quantity of 3,148 units (capacity-constrained), ensuring 95% service level at a modest incremental annual cost.
warnings: Safety stock increased substantially from SAP baseline (208) to recommended (570) — review with planning team before activation.
Order quantity capped at 3,148 due to storage capacity constraint (max_storage_units=3,718.313); unconstrained EOQ was 3,256.
Lead time CV=0.68 classifies as unstable — monitor supplier performance closely.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Continuous demand with high daily volumes and unstable lead times favours continuous-review over periodic-review. The (r,Q) model minimises total annual cost (ordering + holding) via EOQ while providing a statistically grounded reorder point that absorbs both demand and lead-time variability at the 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds: safety_stock(570) + order_quantity(3148) = 3718 units, just within the 3718.313 unit limit. Any upward revision of safety stock (e.g., to the robust estimate of 541+buffer) would require a corresponding reduction in order quantity, increasing ordering frequency and annual ordering cost.
